newsitem.title: USA: AOL mulls new pricing for premium services.
newsitem.headline: AOL mulls new pricing for premium services.

text.p: America Online Inc said it plans to eventually charge more for premium services on the world's largest online service, such as multi-player games.

Steve Case, chairman and CEO of America Online, said at the PC Forum conference here that its $19.95 a month pricing plan is currently the right model, but for premium services, AOL is looking at higher charges.
"We do intend over time to offer premium services, like multi-player games," Case told the conferenence. Multi-player games are computer games where many users are playing together online.

Case declined to be more specific on possible pricing and whether AOL would charge an hourly rate in addition to the $19.95 all-you-can-eat plan, or whether the company would offer, for example, a higher-cost monthly plan for game users. "We haven't announced the pricing yet," Case said afterwards.
Wall Street analysts and some industry executives said they have been expecting AOL to make such move.
Scott Reamer, an analyst at Cowen & Co, said that AOL has been talking about additional charges for premium services in its conference calls with analysts.
"Gaming and business information are the near-term areas they will tackle," Reamer said.

Josh Grotstein, a senior vice president at privately-held Prodigy Services Corp, said the industry has been anticipating AOL to make such a move since it went to flat-rating pricing in December, because game players spend many hours online and some software firms charge licensing fees for use of their games.
"They must be taking a bath by gamers who come online and use the system at a flat rate," Grotstein said.

Prodigy plans to offer tiered pricing on its Prodigy Internet Service soon for multi-player games and financial content, he said. Prodigy Classic, its older, proprietary online service, charges gamers an hourly rate of about $1.50 an hour.

Netcom Communications Services Inc, which in December said it would abandon its flat-rate pricing plan of $19.95 a month, is expected to make its new pricing announcement early this week, as it seeks to focus more on the business market and higher profits.
